subtopic: Kata nama jenis proper common abstract
questionText: Antara berikut, yang manakah kata nama abstrak?
explanation: Kata nama abstrak: keadilan (konsep/bukan fizikal). Malaysia, Ahmad, SMK = kata nama khas/proper.

subtopic: Kata nama jenis proper common abstract
questionText: Antara berikut, yang manakah kata nama khas (proper noun)?
explanation: Sungai Pahang = nama khas (geografi spesifik). sungai/bukit/bandar = kata nama am.

subtopic: Kata nama jenis proper common abstract
questionText: Kata nama 'kebahagiaan' merupakan kata nama jenis:
explanation: Kebahagiaan = abstrak (bukan benda fizikal).

subtopic: Kata ganti nama diri pertama kedua ketiga
questionText: Kata ganti nama diri pertama tunggal ialah:
explanation: Saya = ganti nama diri pertama tunggal. Kami = pertama jamak. Kamu = kedua.

subtopic: Kata ganti nama diri pertama kedua ketiga
questionText: Kata ganti nama diri kedua jamak ialah:
explanation: Kamu semua = ganti nama diri kedua jamak.

questionText: Kata ganti nama tunjuk untuk benda jauh ialah:
explanation: Ini = dekat, itu = jauh (penunjuk).

questionText: Kalimat 'Siapakah guru anda?' mengandungi kata ganti nama:
explanation: Siapakah = kata ganti nama tanya.

questionText: Kata ganti nama orang ketiga tunggal perempuan ialah:
explanation: Beliau = ganti nama orang ketiga tunggal perempuan hormat.

questionText: 'Mereka' dalam ayat 'Mereka pergi ke sekolah' berfungsi sebagai:
explanation: Mereka = ganti nama orang ketiga jamak.

questionText: Ayat 'Ali menulis surat' kepada bentuk pasif menjadi:
explanation: Bentuk pasif: objek jadi subjek; Ali (pelaku) jadi agent.

questionText: Bentuk pasif bagi ayat 'Ibu menggoreng ikan':
explanation: Objek (ikan) jadi subjek dalam bentuk pasif.

questionText: Dalam ayat 'Petani itu menoreh getah', kata kerja 'menoreh' ialah kata kerja:
explanation: Menoreh = transitif (memerlukan objek).

questionText: Ayat 'Kanak-kanak itu berlari di padang' mengandungi kata kerja:
explanation: Berlari = tak transitif (tidak memerlukan objek).

questionText: Ayat pasif yang betul untuk 'Petani menanam padi':
explanation: Objek 'padi' jadi subjek pasif.

questionText: Bentuk terbanding bagi kata sifat 'baik' ialah:
explanation: Terbanding = lebih baik (lebih + adj).

questionText: Bentuk paling tinggi (superlatif) bagi 'tinggi':
explanation: Superlatif: awalan 'ter-' = tertinggi.

questionText: Bentuk perbandingan 'cerdas' adalah:
explanation: Perbandingan = lebih + adj.

questionText: Kata penghubung 'dan', 'atau', 'tetapi' tergolong dalam:
explanation: Hubung gabungan = dan, atau, tetapi, malah, serta.

questionText: Pilih kata hubung yang tepat: 'Saya tidak datang ___ saya sakit.'
explanation: Saya tidak datang kerana saya sakit = sebab. 'Kerana' = kata hubung pancangan sebab.

questionText: 'Dia belajar dengan tekun ___ mendapat keputusan cemerlang.' Pilih kata hubung yang sesuai:
explanation: Lalu = menunjukkan akibat/akibat-akibat. Belajar tekun LALU mendapat keputusan baik = urutan.

questionText: 'Pelajar itu belajar bersungguh-sungguh ___ mendapat keputusan cemerlang.' Kata hubung yang tepat:
explanation: Supaya = tujuan. Pelajar belajar bersungguh-sungguh supaya mendapat keputusan cemerlang.

questionText: Kata bilangan 'pertama', 'kedua', 'ketiga' ialah kata bilangan jenis:
explanation: Ordinal = turutan (pertama, kedua). Kardinal = bilangan (satu, dua).

questionText: 'Sepuluh', 'seratus', 'seribu' adalah kata bilangan:
explanation: Kardinal = bilangan (sepuluh, seratus).

questionText: Perkataan pinjaman yang sudah disesuaikan dengan Bahasa Melayu sepenuhnya:
explanation: Kerusi = pinjaman adaptasi (dari Portuguese 'cadeira'). Computer/software/e-mail = bukan adaptasi.

questionText: Perkataan yang belum disesuaikan dengan ejaan BM:
explanation: Computer belum disesuaikan (asal Inggeris). Lain-lain sudah adaptasi.

questionText: Peribahasa 'Bulat air kerana pembetung' bermaksud:

options.a: Orang yang kembali ke tempat asal

explanation: Bulat air = bulatan air = tempat asal/rumah sendiri. Pembetung = saluran air.

questionText: Peribahasa 'Hendak seribu daya, tak sampai seribu' bermaksud:
explanation: Hendak seribu daya = berusaha dengan kemampuan; tak sampai = gagal. Bermaksud usaha tidak berhasil.

questionText: Peribahasa 'Malu bertanya sesat jalan' bermaksud:

options.a: Jangan malu untuk bertanya jika tidak tahu

explanation: Malu bertanya = segan bertanya. Sesat jalan = tersesat. Bermaksud jangan segan bertanya.

questionText: 'Lemah semangat' merupakan:
explanation: Simpulan bahasa tetap: lemah semangat = tidak bersemangat.

questionText: 'Kera di hutan disusukan, anak di rumah mati kelaparan' merupakan:
explanation: Kera di hutan = tempat jauh. Anak di rumah = sendiri. Peribahasa bermaksud menguruskan orang lain sedangkan sendiri terabaikan.

questionText: Awalan (prefiks) bagi perkataan 'menulis' ialah:
explanation: Awalan me- + tulis = menulis. N- berubah jadi me-.

questionText: Akhiran (sufiks) bagi perkataan 'cantikkan' ialah:
explanation: Akhiran -kan dalam 'cantikkan'. cantum + -kan = cantumkan.

questionText: Apitan (konfiks) bagi perkataan 'keindahan' ialah:
explanation: Apitan: ke- + indah + -an = keindahan.

questionText: Perkataan 'tarian' mengandungi imbuhan:
explanation: Tarian = tari + -an (awalan + akhiran? No). Wait: tarian is tari + -an (akhiran). Tarian: 'tari' + '-an' (akhiran sahaja).

questionText: Perkataan 'kesenian' dibentuk daripada:
explanation: Apitan: ke- + seni + -an = kesenian.

questionText: Awalan 'ber-' dalam perkataan 'bermain' bermaksud:
explanation: Awalan ber- = keadaan/memiliki (bermain = bermain-main).

questionText: Perkataan 'menggajikan' (memberikan pekerjaan kepada) menggunakan imbuhan:
explanation: menggajikan: me- + gaji + -kan = menggajikan (transitif).

questionText: Perkataan pinjaman Inggeris 'gaji' disesuaikan dengan imbuhan Melayu menjadi:
explanation: gaji + me-...-kan = menggajikan (pemberi kerja). Mengerjakan = me- + kerja + -kan. Memperhatikan = me- + per- + hati + -kan. Mengendalikan = me- + kendali + -kan.

questionText: Pilih bentuk kata yang betul:
explanation: Membeli = me- + beli. Kata dasar berakhir vokal i + -i di awal = me-.

questionText: Bentuk yang betul:
explanation: Memasak = me- + masak (kata dasar berakhir konsonan).

questionText: Pilih bentuk kata kerja yang betul:
explanation: Menyanyi = me- + nyanyi (kata dasar vokal i akhir). Menyanyikan = transitif (menyanyi lagu).

questionText: Kata dasar bagi 'mendengar':
explanation: Kata dasar: dengar. Mendengar = meN- + dengar.

questionText: Pecahan perkataan 'membasuh' (kata dasar + imbuhan):
explanation: me- + basuh = membasuh. N- jadi nyaring m-.

questionText: Pecahan bagi perkataan 'menulis':
explanation: Menulis = me- + tulis. N- + tulis ditukar menjadi m- (sebelum huruf t).

questionText: Bentuk jamak bagi 'buku':
explanation: Bentuk jamak: pengulangan (buku-buku).

questionText: 'Kucing-kucing itu' menunjukkan bentuk:
explanation: Kucing-kucing = bentuk jamak.

questionText: Akar kata bagi 'penulisan':
explanation: Penulisan = peN- + tulis + -an. Akar = tulis.

questionText: Akar kata bagi 'persekolahan':
explanation: Persekolahan = peN- + sekolah + -an. Akar = sekolah.

questionText: Pecahan perkataan 'penulisan':
explanation: Apitan: peN- + tulis + -an.

questionText: Pecahan 'keamanan' kepada kata dasar dan imbuhan:
explanation: ke- + aman + -an = keamanan.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Ayat 'Saya sedang membaca buku' menunjukkan bentuk kata kerja:
explanation: Sedang membaca = bentuk kata kerja masa kini/sekarang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Bentuk kata kerja lampau bagi 'pergi':
explanation: Pergi + -lah = perintah (pergilah).

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Ayat 'Esok saya akan pergi ke sekolah' menunjukkan:
explanation: Esok + akan pergi = masa hadapan/akan datang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Ayat 'Saya telah pergi ke sekolah' menunjukkan:
explanation: Telah pergi = peristiwa lampau (masa lampau).

questionText: Pilih bentuk kata kerja perintah yang betul:
explanation: Perintah: duduklah. Tolong duduklah = kata kerja perintah.

questionText: Ayat yang mengandungi kata kerja perintah:
explanation: Masuklah = perintah (akhiran -lah + kata kerja).

questionText: Tukar kepada bentuk aktif: 'Kucing itu dikejar oleh anjing.'
explanation: Bentuk aktif: subjek = agen, objek jadi objek biasa.

questionText: Ayat aktif yang setara dengan 'Surat itu dibaca oleh Ali':
explanation: Pasif 'Surat dibaca Ali' -> aktif 'Ali membaca surat'.

questionText: Bentuk pasif yang betul: 'Kakak membasuh baju':
explanation: Baju (objek) jadi subjek pasif.

questionText: Ayat 'Ali sakit' mengandungi aspek:
explanation: Ali sakit = keadaan (state).

questionText: 'Rumahnya besar' menunjukkan aspek:
explanation: Rumahnya besar = keadaan (kualiti rumah besar).

questionText: Aspek perbuatan ditunjukkan oleh ayat:
explanation: Berlari = perbuatan (action).

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Ayat 'Esok lusa saya akan belajar di perpustakaan' menunjukkan:
explanation: Akan belajar = akan datang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Bentuk kata kerja perintah:
explanation: Bukalah = perintah (kata kerja + -lah).

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: 'Mereka sedang bermain bola' menunjukkan:
explanation: Sedang bermain = sekarang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Ayat 'Saya sudah makan tengah hari' menunjukkan:
explanation: Sudah makan = lampau (sudah = penanda masa lampau).

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Yang mana ayat dengan bentuk sekarang:
explanation: Sedang tidur = sekarang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: 'Esok saya akan berjumpa dengan guru' - bentuk kata kerja:
explanation: Akan bertemu = akan datang.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Pilih ayat dengan bentuk lampau:
explanation: Sudah menonton = lampau.

subtopic: Bentuk kata kerja lampau sekarang akan datang
questionText: Bentuk masa kini untuk 'menulis':
explanation: Masa kini/sekarang = sedang + me-verb.

questionText: Ayat 'Ali belajar' ialah jenis ayat:
explanation: Ayat tunggal: satu subjek + satu predikat.

questionText: 'Ali belajar dan Amin bermain' ialah ayat:
explanation: Gabungan = dua ayat tunggal digabungkan dengan 'dan'.

questionText: 'Ali makan kerana lapar' ialah ayat:
explanation: Pancangan = ada klausa utama + klausa kecil (kerana lapar).

questionText: Susunan songsang: 'Cantik sangat bunga itu' bermaksud:
explanation: Songsang: predikat di depan, subjek di belakang.

questionText: Susunan biasa bagi 'Amat tinggi dia':
explanation: Biasa: subjek (dia) + predikat (amat tinggi).

questionText: 'Buku itu dibacanya' mengandungi kata ganti nama:
explanation: Bacanya = baca + -nya (orang ketiga).

questionText: Ayat alih ganti: 'Buku saya bacakan kepada ibu' bermaksud:
explanation: Alih ganti dengan -kan + nya. Saya membacakan buku.

questionText: 'Siti menulis surat, tetapi adiknya tidak' - jenis ayat:
explanation: Gabungan: dua ayat setara dengan 'tetapi'.

questionText: 'Siti belajar dengan tekun supaya mendapat keputusan cemerlang' - jenis ayat:
explanation: Pancangan: ada tujuan ('supaya') = hubungan tak setara.

questionText: 'Alamak, cantiknya bunga itu!' - jenis ayat:
explanation: Alamak = seruan (ungkapan perasaan).

questionText: 'Betulkah kamu datang ke sekolah semalam?' - jenis ayat:
explanation: Betulkah = ayat tanya (tag -kah).

questionText: Pilih ayat perintah:
explanation: Tolong hantarkan = permintaan sopan = perintah lembut.

questionText: Tanda baca yang digunakan untuk ayat tanya:
explanation: Tanda tanya = ? untuk ayat tanya.

questionText: Tanda baca untuk ayat seruan (pengujaan):
explanation: Seruan = ! (tanda seru).

questionText: Ayat 'Marilah kita belajar dengan tekun' - jenis ayat:
explanation: Marilah = ajakan/perintah lembut.

questionText: Simpulan 'buah hati' bermaksud:
explanation: Buah hati = anak yang disayangi/dikasihi.

questionText: Simpulan 'ringan tangan' bermaksud:
explanation: Ringan tangan = suka memberi/menolong orang lain.

questionText: Simpulan 'keras hati' bermaksud:
explanation: Keras hati = degil/tidak mahu mengalah.

questionText: Simpulan 'besar hati' bermaksud:
explanation: Besar hati = gembira/suka.

questionText: Simpulan 'panas hati' bermaksud:
explanation: Panas hati = marah/berang.

questionText: Ayat 'Bulan tersenyum di langit malam' mengandungi majas:
explanation: Bulan = objek; 'tersenyum' = sifat manusia. Personifikasi = objek diberi sifat manusia.

questionText: Majas personifikasi juga dikenali sebagai:
explanation: Personifikasi = penginsanan (personify = memberi sifat manusia).

questionText: Majas yang membandingkan dua benda secara langsung tanpa kata 'seperti/umpama':
explanation: Metafora = perbandingan langsung (pengibaratan). 'Bunga itu permata di taman'.

questionText: Contoh majas metafora:

options.a: Engkau bagai embun di kaki langit

explanation: Metafora langsung: 'bukan perbandingan dengan seperti'. 'Engkau adalah cahaya mataku'.

questionText: Majas yang membandingkan dua benda dengan kata 'seperti/bagai/umpama':
explanation: Simile = perbandingan dengan kata hubung 'seperti', 'umpama', 'bagaikan'.

questionText: Pilih ayat yang mengandungi simile:
explanation: 'Bagai bulan' = simile (membandingkan wajah dengan bulan).

questionText: Majas yang menggunakan pernyataan berlebihan/lampau:
explanation: Hiperbola = pembesaran/hiperbolis. 'Aku menunggu selama setahun' (waktu sebentar sahaja).

questionText: Contoh hiperbola:
explanation: 'Darah mendidih' = hiperbola (lawan sebenar = darah hanya hangat).

questionText: Majas yang melembutkan/mengecilkan kenyataan:
explanation: Litotes = pernyataan lebih kecil dari sebenar. 'Tidak teruk sangat' = buruk.

questionText: Pilih ayat dengan litotes:
explanation: Litotes: 'tidak berapa menarik' = menarik (melembutkan).

questionText: Majas yang menggunakan perkataan lain untuk menggantikan objek:
explanation: Metonimia = pengganti nama berdasarkan hubungan rapat (contoh: 'Mahkamah' untuk hakim).

questionText: Contoh metonimia:
explanation: 'Mahkamah' = metonimia untuk hakim (menggantikan kata).

questionText: Sinekdoke ialah:
explanation: Sinekdoke = bahagian untuk keseluruhan. 'Semua tangan' = semua orang.

questionText: Contoh sinekdoke:
explanation: 'Semua kepala desa' = orang penting desa (bahagian untuk keseluruhan).

questionText: Majas yang merujuk kepada peristiwa/kejadian terdahulu:
explanation: Alusi = rujukan tidak langsung kepada peristiwa/cerita lampau.

questionText: Contoh alusi:

options.a: Berani kerana benar, takut kerana salah (Hang Tuah)

explanation: Alusi: rujuk kepada pepatah Hang Tuah (cerita lampau).

questionText: Majas yang menggunakan struktur ayat yang seimbang/sejajar:
explanation: Paralelisme = keseimbangan struktur. 'Datang dengan senyuman, pergi dengan kenangan.'

questionText: Pilih contoh paralelisme:

options.a: Masuk dengan niat baik, keluar dengan harapan

explanation: Paralelisme: struktur sejajar 'masuk-niat baik' dan 'keluar-harapan'.

questionText: Majas yang menggunakan perkataan berlawanan:
explanation: Antitesis = pertentangan. 'Miskin di antara kaya, bodoh di antara pandai.'

questionText: Pilih ayat dengan antitesis:

options.a: kaya di waktu muda, miskin di hari tua

explanation: Antitesis: kaya vs miskin, muda vs tua (berlawanan).

questionText: Majas yang mengulangi perkataan di awal ayat/baris:
explanation: Anafora = pengulangan kata di awal. 'Kita harus..., kita harus..., kita harus...'

questionText: Pilih ayat dengan anafora:

options.a: Kita harus belajar, kita harus berusaha, kita harus berjaya

explanation: Anafora: 'kita harus' diulang pada awal setiap klausa.

questionText: Majas yang mengulangi perkataan di akhir ayat/baris:
explanation: Epifora = pengulangan di akhir ayat. 'Saya datang dari..., saya tinggal di..., saya cintai...'

questionText: Pilih ayat dengan epifora:

options.a: Saya suka makan, saya suka minum, saya suka belajar

explanation: Epifora: 'saya suka' di akhir klausa.

questionText: Asonansi = pengulangan:
explanation: Asonansi = ulangan bunyi vokal. Aliterasi = ulangan bunyi konsonan awal.

questionText: Pilih contoh aliterasi:
explanation: Aliterasi: 'B' 'l' diulang pada perkataan 'Bising berlauk-lauk'.

questionText: Onomatopoeia menggunakan perkataan yang meniru bunyi:
explanation: Onomatopoeia = tiruan bunyi. 'Kucing mengeong', 'lonceng berdenting'.

questionText: Pilih contoh onomatopoeia:
explanation: Onomatopoeia: 'berukuk-ukuk' tiruan bunyi monyet.

questionText: Repetisi = pengulangan:
explanation: Repetisi = pengulangan perkataan untuk penekanan/kesan.

questionText: Pilih contoh repetisi:
explanation: Repetisi: 'marilah' diulang 3 kali.

questionText: Oksimoron menggabungkan dua perkataan yang berlawanan:
explanation: Oksimoron = gabungan dua kata berlawanan. 'Suara senyap', 'manis pahit'.

questionText: Pilih contoh oksimoron:
explanation: Oksimoron: 'suara sunyi' (suara + sunyi = berlawanan).

questionText: Paradoks = kenyataan yang seolah-olah bercanggah tetapi sebenarnya:
explanation: Paradoks = bercanggah pada zahir tetapi sebenarnya benar. 'Semakin cepat semakin lambat'.

questionText: Contoh paradoks:
explanation: Paradoks: 'semakin dikurangi, semakin bertambah' (kontradiktif tapi benar dalam konteks tertentu).

questionText: Gaya bahasa pemerian = gaya yang:
explanation: Pemerian = deskripsi/pencitraan dengan kata sifat/perbandingan.

questionText: Pilih ayat gaya pemerian:

options.a: Bunga mawar merah itu harum semerbak di halaman

explanation: Pemerian: 'merah', 'harum semerbak', 'halaman' = deskripsi visual/bau.

questionText: Gaya bahasa perbandingan membandingkan dua hal untuk:
explanation: Perbandingan = mencari persamaan dua hal untuk penjelasan.

questionText: Pilih ayat gaya perbandingan:
explanation: Perbandingan: 'cepatnya seperti kilat' (membandingkan kecepatan).

questionText: Bahasa figuratif merujuk kepada:
explanation: Figuratif = kiasan (majas, peribahasa, simpulan bahasa).

questionText: Pilih contoh bahasa figuratif:
explanation: Figuratif: 'mawar = permata' (perumpamaan).

questionText: Diksi = pilihan kata. Untuk menggantikan kata 'tidak baik', diksi yang lebih halus:
explanation: Diksi halus: 'kurang baik' (lembut).

questionText: Untuk menggantikan 'cantik' dengan diksi yang lebih tepat:
explanation: Diksi halus untuk 'cantik': molek/indah/jelita. 'elok' lebih umum.

questionText: Diksi yang sesuai untuk 'makan banyak':
explanation: 'Menjamu selera' = makan banyak (formal).

questionText: Diksi yang sesuai untuk 'jahil':
explanation: Diksi halus: 'tidak tahu' (lembut).

questionText: Pilih diksi yang paling sesuai dalam karangan rasmi:
explanation: 'Menganjurkan' = formal. 'Membuat majlis' = kurang formal.

questionText: Untuk menggantikan 'pergi' dengan diksi yang lebih tinggi:
explanation: 'Berangkat' = formal untuk 'pergi'. 'Menyusul' = mengikuti.

questionText: Sinonim bagi 'cantik' ialah:
explanation: Sinonim 'cantik' = indah, elok, molek. Kesemua betul.

questionText: Sinonim bagi 'bijaksana' ialah:
explanation: Bijaksana = arif, pandai, cerdas. Kesemua sinonim.

questionText: Sinonim bagi 'cantik' (paling tepat):
explanation: Indah = sinonim tepat untuk cantik. Wangi/harum = bau. Sedap = rasa.

questionText: Antonim bagi 'cantik' ialah:
explanation: Antonim 'cantik' = hodoh, jelik. Kesemua benar.

questionText: Antonim bagi 'pandai' ialah:
explanation: Antonim 'pandai' = bodoh/tolol/dungu. Kesemua antonim.

questionText: Antonim bagi 'rajin' ialah:
explanation: Antonim 'rajin' = malas. Lain-lain bukan antonim.

questionText: Sinonim peribahasa bagi 'Bulat air kerana pembetung':

options.a: Berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing

explanation: Bulat air... = berat sama dipikul, ringan sama dijinjing (kerjasama/tolong-menolong).

questionText: Antonim peribahasa bagi 'Sepandai-pandai tupai melompat, akhirnya jatuh ke tanah juga':
explanation: Sepandai-pandai tupai = kelicikan akhirnya tertangkap. Antonim = biar lambat asalkan selamat (berhati-hati).

questionText: Sinonim bagi 'berlari':
explanation: 'Mengangkah' = berjalan pantas. Sinonim = berlari. 'Berkebat' = berkebat berlari.

questionText: Antonim bagi 'kecil hati' (malu/tidak berani):
explanation: 'Kecil hati' = malu/tidak berani. Antonim = 'besar hati' = berani/gembira.

questionText: Sinonim bagi 'kebahagiaan':
explanation: Kebahagiaan = kesejahteraan, kemakmuran, kesukaan. Sinonim semua.

questionText: Antonim bagi 'keuntungan':
explanation: Antonim 'keuntungan' = kerugian. Lain-lain bukan antonim tepat.

questionText: Perbendaharaan kata sinonim dengan:
explanation: Perbendaharaan kata = kosa kata (vocabulary).

questionText: Untuk 'mahu keluar', diksi yang lebih halus:

questionText: Bacalah petikan: 'Pada suatu pagi, Adi bangun awal. Dia bersiap-siap untuk ke sekolah. Setelah siap, dia berjalan ke sekolah dengan kakaknya.' Apakah yang Adi lakukan pada pagi itu?

explanation: B suka nasi lemak (literal dari dialog).

explanation: To simplify, factor out perfect squares: sqrt(n) = sqrt(sq x rem) = sqrt(sq) x sqrt(rem) = 4sqrt6.
Laws of indices: a^m ÷ a^n = a^(m-n). So 3^3 ÷ 3^2 = 3^1 = 3.

questionText: Find the magnitude of the vector v = (5, 12). #466
explanation: For vector v = (5, 12), magnitude |v| = sqrt((5)^2 + (12)^2) = sqrt(25 + 144) = sqrt169 = 13.

questionText: Simplify log(7) + log(2). #467
explanation: Law of logarithms: log(m) + log(n) = log(m x n). So log(7) + log(2) = log(7 x 2) = log(14).

questionText: What is the centre of the circle (x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 16? #468
explanation: The standard form is (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 where (2, 1) is the centre and r = 4 is the radius. So centre = (2, 1).

questionText: Use the quadratic formula to solve x^2 + 5x - 0 = 0. #469
Find the x-coordinate of the turning point of f(x) = 3x^2 + 2x. #470
explanation: At turning point, f'(x) = 0: 2(3)x + 2 = 0 ⇒ x = -2/6 = -2/6.

questionText: What is sin(30 degrees)? #471
explanation: At 30 degrees, sin = 1/2, cos = sqrt3/2, tan = 1/sqrt3. So sin(30 degrees) = 1/2.

questionText: Calculate 3(5, 4). #472
explanation: Scalar multiplication: 3(5, 4) = (15, 12).

questionText: Convert 45 degrees to radians. #473
explanation: To convert 45 degrees to radians: 45 degrees x pi/180 = 45pi/180 = pi/4 rad.

questionText: Given the linear function f(x) = 3x + 7, find f(5). #474
Find the derivative of f(x) = 4x^4 + 2x^3 + 3. #475
explanation: Apply d/dx[kx^n] = knx^(n-1): f'(x) = 4*4*x^(3) + 2*3*x^(2) + 0 = 16x3 + 6x2. (Constant c differentiates to 0.)

questionText: Find the derivative of f(x) = 3x^3 + 5x^3 + 1. #476
explanation: Apply d/dx[kx^n] = knx^(n-1): f'(x) = 3*3*x^(2) + 5*3*x^(2) + 0 = 9x2 + 15x2. (Constant c differentiates to 0.)

questionText: Use the quadratic formula to solve x^2 - 3x - 0 = 0. #477
Find the magnitude of the vector v = (3, 4). #478
explanation: For vector v = (3, 4), magnitude |v| = sqrt((3)^2 + (4)^2) = sqrt(9 + 16) = sqrt25 = 5.

questionText: In a right triangle, the opposite side = 5 and the adjacent side = 8. Find tan theta. #479
explanation: In a right triangle with opposite = 5, adjacent = 8: tan theta = opposite/adjacent = 5/8 = 0.62.

questionText: Given f(u) = 2u + 1 and g(v) = v^2, find f(g(1)). #480
explanation: Let f(u) = 2u + 1 and g(v) = v^2. Then f(g(x)) = f(1) = 2(1) + 1 = 3.

questionText: What is the centre of the circle (x - 0)^2 + (y - 0)^2 = 9? #481
explanation: The standard form is (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 where (0, 0) is the centre and r = 3 is the radius. So centre = (0, 0).

questionText: Find the gradient of the curve f(x) = x^2 - 5x at the point where x = 4. #482
explanation: f(x) = x^2 - 5x. Differentiate: f'(x) = 2x + -5. At x = 4: f'(4) = 2(4) + -5 = 3.

questionText: Simplify log(3) + log(3). #483
explanation: Law of logarithms: log(m) + log(n) = log(m x n). So log(3) + log(3) = log(3 x 3) = log(9).

questionText: Find the x-coordinate of the turning point of f(x) = 2x^2 - 2x. #484
explanation: At turning point, f'(x) = 0: 2(2)x + -2 = 0 ⇒ x = 2/4 = 2/4.

questionText: Find the distance between points (1, 1) and (4, 6). #485
explanation: Distance d = sqrt((x₂-x₁)^2 + (y₂-y₁)^2) = sqrt((4-1)^2 + (6-1)^2) = sqrt(9 + 25) = sqrt34 = 5.83 units.

questionText: Use the quadratic formula to solve x^2 - 5x + 4 = 0. #486
Integrate: ∫(3x^2 + 4x + 1) dx. #487
Find the gradient of the curve f(x) = x^2 + 2x at the point where x = 4. #488
explanation: f(x) = x^2 + 2x. Differentiate: f'(x) = 2x + 2. At x = 4: f'(4) = 2(4) + 2 = 10.

questionText: What is cos(60 degrees)? #489
explanation: At 60 degrees, sin = sqrt3/2, cos = 1/2, tan = sqrt3. So cos(60 degrees) = 1/2.

questionText: Given the linear function f(x) = -1x + -1, find f(1). #490
Evaluate log₂(16). #491
explanation: log₂(16) = ? means 2^x = 16. Since 2^4 = 16, x = 4. So log₂(16) = 4.

questionText: Find the median of: 4, 5, 10, 11, 14. #492
explanation: Median = middle value when data is sorted in ascending order. Sorted: 4, 5, 10, 11, 14. Middle value (3rd of 5) = 10.

questionText: Find the area of a sector with radius 4 cm and angle 60 degrees at the centre. #493
explanation: Sector area A = ½ x r^2 x theta = ½ x 4^2 x 60pi/180 = ½ x 16 x 1.0472 = 8.378 cm^2.

questionText: What is the centre of the circle (x - 2)^2 + (y - 1)^2 = 16? #494
explanation: The standard form is (x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2 where (2, 1) is the centre and r = 4 is the radius. So centre = (2, 1).

questionText: Given the linear function f(x) = -1x + 0, find f(-2). #495
Find y on the line y = -2x + -3 when x = 1. #496
Solve log_2(x) = 3. #497
explanation: Solve log_2(x) = 3. This means 2^3 = x, so x = 8.

questionText: A quadratic equation has roots -4 and 5. Find the sum and product of the roots. #498
explanation: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with roots alpha, beta: alpha + beta = -b/a, alphabeta = c/a. Here roots are -4 and 5. Sum = -4 + 5 = 1, product = -4 x 5 = -20.

questionText: Integrate: ∫10 dx. #499
explanation: ∫10 dx = 10x + C. (Verified against KSSM Form 4 Additional Mathematics standard formula.)

questionText: A quadratic equation has roots 2 and 1. Find the sum and product of the roots. #500
explanation: For ax^2 + bx + c = 0 with roots alpha, beta: alpha + beta = -b/a, alphabeta = c/a. Here roots are 2 and 1. Sum = 2 + 1 = 3, product = 2 x 1 = 2.

subtopic: Hypothesis formulation if then testable statement
questionText: In a biological experiment, which is the correct form to write a scientific hypothesis?

options.a: If [variable X], then [outcome Y] will occur
options.b: Plants grow because they are green

explanation: A valid hypothesis must be testable in 'If... then...' form.

questionText: When investigating the effect of light on plant growth, what should be kept the same (controlled) throughout?

options.a: Amount of water given to plants
options.d: Time of day natural light changes

explanation: Controlled variables (water, soil, temperature) must stay constant to isolate light effect.

subtopic: Data analysis line graph gradient interpretation
questionText: A line graph shows distance (m) on y-axis and time (s) on x-axis. What does the gradient represent?
explanation: Gradient of distance-time graph = change in distance ÷ change in time = speed.

questionText: Which is the correct way to draw a biology specimen in a lab report?

options.a: Use clear lines with accurate proportions and labels

explanation: Standard scientific drawing requires accurate proportions, clear lines, no shading, with labels.

questionText: When handling concentrated acid in a T4 chemistry lab, which safety equipment is essential?

options.d: Open the bottle near face to smell

explanation: Concentrated acid requires goggles, gloves, and fume cupboard for safety.

subtopic: Scientific theory vs hypothesis vs law distinction
questionText: Which is the correct difference between a scientific theory and a hypothesis?

options.a: Theory is well-tested and supported; hypothesis is untested or initial
options.b: Theory is untested; hypothesis is proven
options.d: Theory and hypothesis mean the same

explanation: Hypothesis = testable prediction; theory = well-supported by many experiments.

questionText: A student says 'The Petri dish is warm, so bacteria are growing.' Which is the inference?
explanation: Inference = explanation/interpretation. Observation = fact noticed. Warm = observation; bacteria growing = inference.

questionText: Why is random sampling preferred over convenience sampling in ecological studies?
explanation: Random sampling = each member of population has equal chance = representative + unbiased.

subtopic: Mean median mode statistical analysis choice
questionText: In T4 class test scores, which average is most affected by one extreme value (outlier)?
explanation: Mean = sum/affected by outliers. Median = middle value (less affected).

questionText: If a T4 measurement is given as 25 ± 1 mm, what does the ±1 indicate?
explanation: ± value = uncertainty range (measurement error or standard deviation).

subtopic: Cell cycle mitosis phases prophase metaphase anaphase telophase
questionText: During which phase of mitosis do sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles?
explanation: Anaphase = sister chromatids pulled apart to opposite poles of cell.

subtopic: Cell cycle G1 S G2 M phase regulation
questionText: What happens during the S phase of the cell cycle?
explanation: S phase (Synthesis) = DNA replication (genetic material doubled before division).

subtopic: Mitosis versus meiosis comparison genetic variation
questionText: Which is a key difference between mitosis and meiosis?

options.a: Meiosis produces 4 genetically different haploid cells

explanation: Meiosis = 4 haploid gametes (genetically varied). Mitosis = 2 identical diploid cells.

questionText: What distinguishes a malignant tumour from a benign tumour?

options.a: Malignant tumours invade surrounding tissues and metastasise
options.b: Benign tumours spread to other organs

explanation: Malignant = cancer cells invade + spread (metastasise). Benign = localised, non-invasive.

subtopic: Stem cell pluripotent multipotent medical therapy
questionText: Why are stem cells important in medical research?

options.a: Can differentiate into many specialised cell types

explanation: Stem cells = undifferentiated; can become specialised (e.g., for organ repair).

questionText: What is apoptosis?

options.b: Random cell death due to injury

explanation: Apoptosis = programmed, controlled cell death (normal part of life, e.g., tadpole tail).

subtopic: Enzyme specificity lock and key induced fit model
questionText: Which model best describes enzyme substrate binding?

options.a: Induced fit model (enzyme moulds to substrate)

explanation: Induced fit model = enzyme active site moulds slightly to substrate (better fit than rigid lock-key).

questionText: How does a competitive inhibitor affect enzyme activity?

options.a: Binds to active site, blocks substrate binding

explanation: Competitive inhibitor = competes with substrate for the active site.

questionText: How does a non-competitive inhibitor bind to an enzyme?

options.a: Binds to a site other than the active site (allosteric)
options.b: Binds to the active site competing with substrate

explanation: Non-competitive inhibitor binds to allosteric site, changes enzyme shape.

subtopic: Protein synthesis transcription mRNA production nucleus
questionText: Where does transcription occur in a eukaryotic cell?
explanation: Transcription (DNA → mRNA) occurs in the nucleus (in eukaryotes).

questionText: What is the role of ribosomes in translation?

options.a: Assemble amino acids into polypeptides using mRNA template

explanation: Ribosomes = site of translation (mRNA codon read → amino acid chain).

subtopic: Codon three nucleotides amino acid code
questionText: What does a codon in mRNA consist of?
explanation: Codon = 3 mRNA nucleotides specifying one amino acid.

subtopic: Gene mutation types point frameshift chromosomal
questionText: What is a point mutation?

options.a: A change in a single nucleotide base

explanation: Point mutation = single base change (substitution). Frameshift = insertion/deletion.

questionText: How does a frameshift mutation affect the resulting protein?

options.a: Changes all amino acids after it (different protein)

explanation: Frameshift = insertion/deletion shifts reading frame → changes downstream amino acids.

questionText: Which condition is caused by aneuploidy (abnormal chromosome number)?
explanation: Down syndrome = trisomy 21 (extra chromosome 21) = aneuploidy.

questionText: In a plant cell, which organelle is responsible for photosynthesis?
explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll which absorbs light energy for photosynthesis (6CO₂ + 6H₂O -> C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂). Mitochondria produce ATP via respiration; ribosomes synthesise proteins; the Golgi apparatus packages proteins for secretion.

subtopic: Genetic disorder autosomal dominant recessive example
questionText: Which is an example of an autosomal recessive disorder in humans?
explanation: Cystic fibrosis = autosomal recessive (gene on chromosome 7).

questionText: In a pedigree chart showing a recessive trait affecting both males and females equally, what is the most likely inheritance pattern?
explanation: Autosomal recessive = affects both sexes equally = typical pedigree pattern.

subtopic: Hormone action specificity receptor target cell
questionText: Why do hormones only affect specific target cells?

options.a: Only target cells have matching receptors for that hormone
options.c: Hormones are produced only near target cells
options.d: All cells respond to all hormones

explanation: Hormone specificity = target cells have specific receptors that recognise the hormone.

questionText: What is the function of a second messenger (e.g., cAMP) in cell signalling?

options.a: Amplifies the hormone signal inside the cell
options.b: Is the first signal at the receptor

explanation: Second messenger (cAMP) = amplifies signal from cell-surface receptor to cell interior.

subtopic: Meiosis I vs Meiosis II difference
questionText: In meiosis, what separates during Anaphase I?
explanation: Meiosis I = homologous pairs separate. Meiosis II = sister chromatids separate (like mitosis).

subtopic: Crossing over prophase I genetic recombination
questionText: What is the evolutionary advantage of crossing over during meiosis?
explanation: Crossing over = exchanges DNA between homologous chromosomes = genetic variation.

questionText: What is nondisjunction?

options.a: Failure of chromosomes to separate properly during meiosis

explanation: Nondisjunction = chromosomes fail to separate → gametes have wrong chromosome number.

questionText: What is the sex chromosome pattern in Klinefelter syndrome?
explanation: Klinefelter = XXY (male phenotype with extra X chromosome).

questionText: What is the sex chromosome pattern in Turner syndrome?
explanation: Turner = XO (female missing one X chromosome).

questionText: Why is mitochondrial DNA inherited only from the mother?

options.a: Sperm mitochondria are destroyed after fertilisation

explanation: Sperm mitochondria are tagged for destruction after fusion with egg; only egg's mtDNA inherited.

questionText: Why is cytochrome c useful in evolutionary studies?

options.a: It is highly conserved across species with small variations
options.b: It changes randomly in all species

explanation: Cytochrome c amino acid differences reflect evolutionary divergence between species.

questionText: What is the role of a tumour suppressor gene?

options.a: Controls cell division; prevents uncontrolled growth when functioning

explanation: Tumour suppressor genes (e.g., p53) = brake on cell division; mutations lead to cancer.

questionText: Why do telomeres shorten with each cell division?

options.a: DNA replication cannot fully copy chromosome ends
options.d: Telomeres are not part of DNA

explanation: End-replication problem: DNA polymerase cannot fully replicate ends → telomeres shorten with age.

subtopic: PCR polymerase chain reaction DNA amplification
questionText: What is the function of PCR (polymerase chain reaction)?

options.a: Amplifies specific DNA regions for analysis

explanation: PCR = in vitro DNA amplification using heat cycles + Taq polymerase + primers.

questionText: In gel electrophoresis, smaller DNA fragments move:

options.a: Faster and further through the gel

explanation: Smaller fragments pass through gel pores faster → travel further from wells.

questionText: What is recombinant DNA technology?

options.a: Combining DNA from different sources into one molecule

explanation: Recombinant DNA = inserting foreign DNA into host genome (basis of genetic engineering).

questionText: What is the function of a restriction enzyme?

options.a: Cuts DNA at specific nucleotide sequences

explanation: Restriction enzymes = molecular scissors that cut DNA at specific palindromic sequences.

subtopic: DNA ligase function joining Okazaki fragments
questionText: What is the role of DNA ligase?

options.a: Joins DNA fragments together (forms phosphodiester bonds)

explanation: DNA ligase = joins Okazaki fragments on lagging strand during DNA replication.

subtopic: Insulin genetically engineered production yeast bacteria
questionText: Why is insulin produced by genetically engineered bacteria?

options.a: Cheaper, purer, no risk of animal disease transmission

explanation: Recombinant insulin from E. coli = cheaper, purer, no animal-sourced contamination risk.

subtopic: Genetically modified organism Bt corn example
questionText: What is the benefit of Bt corn (containing Bacillus thuringiensis gene)?

options.a: Resistant to certain insect pests, reducing pesticide use

explanation: Bt corn = expresses bacterial toxin → resists pests → less pesticide needed.

subtopic: Sickle cell anaemia point mutation codominant
questionText: What type of mutation causes sickle cell anaemia?
explanation: Sickle cell = single base substitution in β-globin gene (GAG → GTG, Glu → Val).

questionText: How does the sickle cell allele provide a survival advantage in malaria-endemic regions?

options.a: Heterozygous (HbAHbS) individuals are more resistant to malaria
options.b: Heterozygous individuals are immune to all diseases

explanation: Heterozygous advantage = HbAHbS confers malaria resistance while still able to carry oxygen.

questionText: Why is DNA fingerprinting useful in forensic identification?

options.a: Each person (except identical twins) has unique DNA patterns

explanation: DNA fingerprinting uses unique VNTR/STR regions → individual identification (except monozygotic twins).

subtopic: Cloning somatic cell nuclear transfer basic
questionText: Which cellular organelle is known as the powerhouse of the cell and produces ATP through aerobic respiration?
explanation: Mitochondria are called the 'powerhouse of the cell' because they generate ATP (adenosine triphosphate) through aerobic respiration (glucose + oxygen -> CO2 + water + energy). The nucleus contains DNA; ribosomes synthesise proteins; the endoplasmic reticulum transports materials.

questionText: What is one piece of evidence for maternal inheritance of mitochondrial DNA?

options.a: Children's mtDNA always matches mother's mtDNA exactly
options.b: Children's mtDNA always matches father's mtDNA
options.c: mtDNA sequence is random in family

explanation: Mitochondrial inheritance evidence: offspring mtDNA matches mother (not father).

questionText: Which condition would denature an enzyme permanently?
explanation: Very high temperature (or extreme pH) = denaturation = permanent change in shape.

questionText: Pepsin works best in the stomach because:

options.a: It has an optimum pH of about 2 (acidic)
options.c: It is not affected by pH

explanation: Pepsin (stomach protease) has optimum pH ~2 (matches stomach acid).

questionText: Most human enzymes have an optimum temperature of approximately:
explanation: Most human enzymes work best at body temperature (~37°C).

subtopic: Denaturation enzyme shape active site lost
questionText: When an enzyme is denatured, what happens to its shape and active site?

options.a: Permanent loss of tertiary structure; active site cannot bind substrate

explanation: Denaturation = irreversible shape change; active site no longer fits substrate.

questionText: What is the role of a coenzyme (e.g., vitamin B)?

options.a: Aids enzyme function without being part of enzyme structure

explanation: Coenzymes (often vitamins) assist enzyme reactions without being the enzyme's amino acids.

questionText: How do cells receive specific signals only from certain hormones?

options.a: Only cells with matching receptors can respond
options.b: All cells respond to all hormones equally

explanation: Hormone specificity = cell-surface or intracellular receptors unique to signal.

questionText: Which is an example of negative feedback in humans?

options.a: High blood glucose → insulin released → glucose lowered
options.b: High body temp → body further heats up
options.c: Eating sugar → sugar level rises forever

explanation: Negative feedback = response to stimulus reduces original stimulus (glucose regulation).

questionText: Why is body temperature regulation (37°C) important for enzyme activity?

options.a: Enzymes work best at optimum temperature (37°C)
options.c: Body temperature is unrelated to enzymes

explanation: Most body enzymes have optimum 37°C → body maintains this temperature for best function.

questionText: What is the main function of the kidney in osmoregulation?

options.a: Regulate water and salt balance in the body

explanation: Kidneys filter blood, reabsorb water/salts, excrete waste → water balance.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: In the Periodic Table, what does the period number indicate?

options.a: Number of electron shells in the atom

explanation: Period number = number of occupied electron shells (1-7).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Periodic table group I II VII VIII meaning
questionText: Elements in Group I of the Periodic Table share the property of:

options.a: Having 1 electron in their outermost shell

explanation: Group I (alkali metals): 1 outer electron → highly reactive + form +1 ions.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Atomic radius trend across period down group
questionText: How does atomic radius change across a period (left to right)?
explanation: Across period: nuclear charge increases but shielding stays similar → atomic radius decreases.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: How does first ionization energy change across a period?
explanation: Across period: stronger nuclear attraction → higher ionization energy (with some dips).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: What does electronegativity measure?

options.a: Atom's ability to attract bonding electrons

explanation: Electronegativity = atom's pull on shared electrons in a bond (Pauling scale).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Across Period 3, which type of element generally has the highest melting point?
explanation: Giant covalent structures (Si, SiO₂) have very high melting points due to many strong bonds.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: In the reactivity series, which is the MOST reactive metal?
explanation: K (potassium) > Na > Ca > Mg > Al > Zn > Fe > (H) > Cu (most reactive → least).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: When zinc is placed in copper(II) sulfate solution, what is observed?

options.a: Blue solution fades; reddish copper coats zinc
options.d: Zinc dissolves with no metal deposit

explanation: Zn + CuSO₄ → ZnSO₄ + Cu (more reactive Zn displaces Cu). Blue → colourless; Cu deposits.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Transition elements variable oxidation states coloured compounds
questionText: Why are transition element compounds often coloured?

options.a: Due to d-electron transitions absorbing visible light

explanation: Transition metals have partially-filled d shells → d-d electronic transitions → visible colour.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Why is iron used as a catalyst in the Haber process?

options.a: Provides large surface area; lowers activation energy

explanation: Iron catalyst (Fe) speeds up N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ without being consumed.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Noble gases inert unreactive octet stable
questionText: Why are noble gases (Group 18) largely unreactive?

options.a: They have a stable full outer electron shell (octet)

explanation: Noble gases have full valence shells → stable → rarely react.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: How does reactivity change down Group VII (halogens)?

options.a: Decreases (atomic radius increases, electron attraction decreases)

explanation: Down Group VII: atomic size ↑, outer shell further from nucleus → less able to attract e⁻ → reactivity ↓.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Period 3 oxide type acidic basic amphoteric
questionText: Sodium oxide (Na₂O) reacts with water to form:
explanation: Na₂O + H₂O → 2NaOH (basic oxide dissolves to give alkali).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Sulfur dioxide (SO₂) reacts with water to form:
explanation: SO₂ + H₂O → H₂SO₃ (sulfurous acid, acidic oxide).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Aluminium oxide is described as amphoteric because it:

options.a: Reacts with both acids and bases

explanation: Al₂O₃ + acid or + base = amphoteric (e.g., Al₂O₃ + 6HCl → 2AlCl₃ + 3H₂O).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Atomic number proton count element identity
questionText: How is the identity of an element uniquely determined?

options.a: By the number of protons in its nucleus
options.c: By its electron number alone always
options.d: By the number of neutrons only

explanation: Atomic number = proton count; unique Z identifies the element (e.g., Z=6 = carbon).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Mass number (A) of an atom equals:
explanation: Mass number = sum of protons + neutrons (electrons have negligible mass).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Which describes isotopes of the same element?

options.c: Same atomic number, different chemical symbols

explanation: Isotopes = same element (same Z), different A (different neutrons).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: What does relative atomic mass of an element represent?

options.a: Weighted average mass of isotopes considering abundance

explanation: Relative atomic mass = weighted average of all isotopes based on natural abundance.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Chlorine water can displace which halide from its salt solution?
explanation: More reactive Cl₂ displaces less reactive Br₂ and I₂ from their salt solutions.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Metal oxide basicity trend down group I
questionText: Down Group I (alkali metals), the metal oxides become:
explanation: Down Group I: metal character increases → oxide becomes more strongly basic.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Sodium chloride (NaCl) is a typical ionic compound. Silicon tetrachloride (SiCl₄) is:

options.b: An ionic compound with high melting point

explanation: SiCl₄ has Si (semi-metal) + Cl (non-metal) → covalent bonding. NaCl has metal+non-metal → ionic.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Why does sodium have a relatively low melting point (98°C) compared to silicon (1410°C)?

options.a: Na is metallic with weak delocalised bonds; Si is giant covalent
options.c: Si has weak van der Waals forces

explanation: Na = giant metallic (weak delocalised e⁻ bonds) → low mp. Si = giant covalent (strong Si-Si bonds) → high mp.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Pure silicon is described as a semiconductor because:

options.a: Its conductivity is between metal and insulator
options.b: It conducts like a metal at all temperatures
options.c: It does not conduct at all
options.d: It is highly reactive with water

explanation: Semiconductor = poor conductor at low temp, good at high temp (or when doped). Silicon = classic example.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Reactivity Group I alkali metal water reaction
questionText: Which observation is correct when potassium reacts with water?

options.a: Floats, melts, burns with lilac flame, alkaline solution forms

explanation: K + H₂O → KOH + H₂↑ (sizzles, lilac flame due to K⁺ emission).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
questionText: Iron can exist in oxidation states +2 and +3. Why is this?

options.a: Transition metals have variable oxidation states from d-orbital configurations

explanation: Fe has multiple accessible oxidation states (Fe²⁺ / Fe³⁺) due to d-electron arrangements.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Transition element coloured ion copper blue
questionText: Copper(II) sulfate solution is blue because Cu²⁺ ions:
explanation: Cu²⁺ d-d electron transitions absorb specific wavelengths (orange-red) → remaining colour seen is blue.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Period 3 element oxide acidic basic amphoteric
questionText: Which Period 3 oxide is amphoteric?
explanation: Al₂O₃ is amphoteric (reacts with both acids and bases).

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Group VIII noble gas electronic configuration
questionText: Why do noble gases not form ions easily?

options.a: They have full outer electron shells (stable octet)

explanation: Noble gases already have full valence shell → no tendency to gain/lose e⁻.

topic: Chemistry - Periodic Table and Periodic Trends
subtopic: Periodicity across period 3 basic to acidic
questionText: Across Period 3, how does oxide character change from Na to Cl?
explanation: Na₂O basic → MgO basic → Al₂O₃ amphoteric → SiO₂/P₄O₁₀/SO₃/Cl₂O → acidic.

subtopic: Ionic bonding electron transfer metal nonmetal
questionText: Ionic bonding typically forms between:
explanation: Ionic bond = metal (loses e⁻) + non-metal (gains e⁻) → cation + anion.

questionText: Covalent bonding typically occurs between:
explanation: Covalent bond = 2 non-metals share electrons (e.g., H-O in H₂O).

subtopic: Sodium chloride ionic bond electron dot diagram
questionText: How many electrons does each Na atom transfer to each Cl atom in NaCl ionic bond?
explanation: Na (1 outer e⁻) loses 1 → Na⁺. Cl (7 outer e⁻) gains 1 → Cl⁻.

subtopic: Metallic bonding delocalised electrons sea model
questionText: What holds metal atoms together in a metallic bond?

options.a: Delocalised electrons in 'sea' around positive ions

explanation: Metallic bond = 'sea' of delocalised electrons surrounding positive metal ions.

subtopic: Bond polarity electronegativity difference polar nonpolar
questionText: When electronegativity difference between atoms is greater than 1.7, the bond is typically:
explanation: ΔEN > 1.7 = ionic. 0.4-1.7 = polar covalent. < 0.4 = non-polar covalent.

questionText: Why is the O-H bond in water polar?

options.a: Oxygen has higher electronegativity → pulls electrons

explanation: O (EN 3.5) more electronegative than H (EN 2.1) → O pulls electrons → bond is polar.

questionText: How is a dative (coordinate) bond different from a normal covalent bond?

options.a: Both electrons come from one atom only
options.b: Electrons come from both atoms equally

explanation: Dative bond = one atom (donor) provides BOTH electrons; other (acceptor) provides none.

subtopic: Intermolecular forces van der Waals dispersion
questionText: What causes van der Waals forces between molecules?

options.a: Temporary dipoles from uneven electron distribution

explanation: Van der Waals = temporary dipoles (instantaneous uneven e⁻ distribution) cause attraction.

subtopic: Permanent dipole dipole forces example HCl
questionText: Which substance has permanent dipole-permanent dipole forces between molecules (besides H₂O)?
explanation: HCl is polar (Cl more electronegative than H) → permanent dipole-dipole attractions.

subtopic: Hydrogen bonding water properties high boiling
questionText: Why does water have an unusually high boiling point (100°C)?

options.a: Hydrogen bonding between H₂O molecules requires extra energy to break

explanation: H-bonds (O-H···O) are strong → require extra energy to overcome → high boiling point.

subtopic: Properties comparison ionic versus covalent compounds
questionText: Which property is typical of ionic compounds (e.g., NaCl)?

options.a: High melting point, conducts electricity when molten
options.b: Low melting point, soluble in organic solvents

explanation: Ionic compounds = high mp, conduct when molten/dissolved (mobile ions), brittle.

subtopic: Properties covalent compounds low melting point
questionText: A substance has low melting point, does not conduct electricity in any state. This substance is likely:
explanation: Covalent molecular = low mp + poor conductor (no free ions/electrons).

questionText: Why is diamond extremely hard and has very high melting point?

options.a: Each carbon bonds covalently to 4 others in giant structure
options.c: It has weak van der Waals

explanation: Diamond = giant covalent lattice of C atoms, each bonded to 4 other C (strong covalent).

questionText: Why are metals malleable and ductile?

options.a: Layers of positive ions can slide over each other (delocalised e⁻ 'glue')
options.d: Layers are strongly held in place

explanation: Metallic bond = layers of +ions in delocalised electron sea → layers slide → malleability.

questionText: Why do ionic compounds dissolve in water but not in hexane?

options.a: Water is polar; ionic charges are attracted to water molecules

explanation: Polar water dissolves ionic compounds (ion-dipole attractions). Hexane non-polar ≠ effective.

questionText: For H-Cl bond, electronegativity values are H=2.2, Cl=3.0. The bond type is:
explanation: Electronegativity is the ability of an atom to attract shared electrons in a covalent bond. The larger the electronegativity difference between two atoms, the more polar (or ionic) the bond. For example, Na-Cl bond (electronegativity difference 2.23) is ionic; H-Cl (1.31) is polar covalent; Cl-Cl (0) is pure covalent.

questionText: How many bonding pairs of electrons are shown around the carbon atom in CO₂ (O=C=O)?
explanation: O=C=O has 2 double bonds = 4 shared pairs around carbon.

questionText: Which bond in NH₄⁺ is a coordinate (dative) bond?

options.a: The N-H bond formed when NH₃ donates lone pair to H⁺
options.c: Only one of the N-H bonds from original NH₃

explanation: NH₃ donates lone pair to H⁺ → dative bond forms (4th N-H bond).

questionText: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a C=C double bond?
explanation: Double bond = 2 shared pairs (4 e⁻ total).

questionText: How many electron pairs are shared in a triple bond?
explanation: Triple bond = 3 shared pairs (6 e⁻).

questionText: Why does HF have a higher boiling point than HCl despite HCl being heavier?

options.a: H-F forms hydrogen bonds (F is highly electronegative)

explanation: HF forms H-bonds (F very electronegative, small size) → strong IMF → higher bp.

questionText: Why does silicon dioxide (SiO₂) have a very high melting point?

options.a: Giant covalent structure with strong Si-O bonds

explanation: SiO₂ (sand) = giant covalent, all atoms joined by strong covalent bonds throughout.

subtopic: Giant metallic structure use electrical wiring
questionText: Why are metals good conductors of electricity?

options.a: Free delocalised electrons can carry charge through metal

explanation: Metallic bonding = delocalised electrons; these mobile electrons carry electric current.

questionText: When does solid sodium chloride conduct electricity?

options.a: Only when molten or dissolved in water (ions free to move)

explanation: Solid NaCl: ions fixed in lattice (no conduction). Molten/dissolved: ions move = conduction.

subtopic: Giant covalent structure graphite electrical conductor
questionText: Why does graphite conduct electricity but diamond does not?

options.a: Graphite has delocalised electrons between layers; diamond does not

explanation: Graphite = layers with delocalised e⁻ between; can conduct in-plane. Diamond = all electrons localised.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Brønsted-Lowry acid proton donor base acceptor
questionText: According to Brønsted-Lowry, an acid is:
explanation: Brønsted-Lowry acid = proton (H⁺) donor; base = proton (H⁺) acceptor.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Lewis acid electron pair acceptor definition
questionText: According to Lewis, an acid is:
explanation: Lewis acid = electron pair acceptor (broader definition than Brønsted-Lowry).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: HCl strong acid complete ionisation rate
questionText: Why is hydrochloric acid (HCl) classified as a strong acid in water?

options.a: HCl fully dissociates into H⁺ and Cl⁻ ions

explanation: HCl fully ionises (dissociates) in water producing a high concentration of H⁺ ions; this complete ionisation defines a strong acid.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: A 0.1 M solution of ethanoic acid has a higher pH than 0.1 M HCl because ethanoic acid:
explanation: Weak acid → fewer H⁺ ions released → higher pH (less acidic).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Salt preparation acid metal zinc sulfate
questionText: Which method is used to prepare zinc sulfate salt in a laboratory?
explanation: Zn + H₂SO₄ → ZnSO₄ + H₂↑ (metal + acid = salt + hydrogen).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Salt preparation insoluble base copper(II) oxide
questionText: How would you prepare copper(II) sulfate salt in the laboratory safely?
explanation: Insoluble base + warm dilute acid → filter excess solid → crystallise filtrate → salt crystals.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Salt preparation acid carbonate sodium chloride
questionText: How is sodium chloride prepared in the laboratory?
explanation: Acid + alkali → salt + water. Evaporate to crystallise salt: NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H₂O.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: A salt formed from a strong acid and weak alkali produces a solution that is:
explanation: Strong acid + weak alkali → salt of strong acid + weak base → hydrolyses acidic.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: What is the pH of ammonium chloride (NH₄Cl) solution?
explanation: NH₄Cl ⇌ NH₄⁺ + Cl⁻; NH₄⁺ hydrolyses releasing H⁺ → acidic.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Sodium ethanoate (CH₃COONa) in water gives:
explanation: CH₃COONa from weak acid + strong alkali → salt hydrolyses basic.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Buffer action against small pH change
questionText: How does a buffer solution behave when a small amount of acid is added?
explanation: Buffer = mixture of weak acid + its salt (or weak base + salt) → resists pH change.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Buffer in blood bicarbonate carbonic acid
questionText: The carbonic acid-hydrogencarbonate buffer in blood helps maintain pH at about:
explanation: Blood buffer (H₂CO₃/HCO₃⁻) maintains blood pH ≈ 7.4 (critical for life).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Acid base titration standard solution calculation
questionText: In a titration, 25.0 cm³ of 0.1 M NaOH is neutralised by 25.0 cm³ of HCl. What is the concentration of HCl?
explanation: At neutralisation: NaOH moles = HCl moles; equal volumes → equal concentrations → 0.1 M.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Which indicator would be most suitable for a strong acid - strong alkali titration (e.g., HCl + NaOH)?

options.a: Any with transition range pH 3-11 (e.g., methyl orange or phenolphthalein)

explanation: Strong acid + strong base titration = sharp pH jump across wide range → either indicator suitable.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Weak acid strong base titration indicator methyl orange
questionText: For weak acid + strong base titration (e.g., CH₃COOH + NaOH), the most suitable indicator is:
explanation: Weak acid + strong base: equivalence point pH > 7 → phenolphthalein suitable.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Which apparatus is used to deliver a precisely measured variable volume in titration?
explanation: Burette = graduated glass tube with stopcock → variable measured volume. Pipette = fixed volume.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: What is observed at the endpoint of an acid-base titration?
explanation: Endpoint = first permanent colour change (indicator). Equivalence point = stoichiometric neutralisation.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: 25.0 cm³ of NaOH solution requires 20.0 cm³ of 0.10 M HCl for neutralisation. What is [NaOH]?
explanation: Moles HCl = 0.020 × 0.10 = 0.002. Same moles NaOH. [NaOH] = 0.002/0.025 = 0.08 M.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: When diluting concentrated sulfuric acid, you should:

options.a: Always add acid to water, not water to acid
options.c: Mix both at the same time

explanation: Acid to water = acid sinks, heat dissipated safely. Water to acid = violent boiling + splash (dangerous).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: How do you test for a carbonate ion (CO₃²⁻) in an unknown salt?

options.a: Add dilute acid → effervescence (CO₂ gas, limewater turns milky)

explanation: Carbonate + acid → CO₂↑ → CO₂ turns limewater (Ca(OH)₂) milky.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Adding sodium carbonate solution to a solution containing lead(II) ions produces:
explanation: Pb²⁺(aq) + CO₃²⁻(aq) → PbCO₃(s) (white insoluble carbonate).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: How do you test for sulfate ion (SO₄²⁻)?

options.a: Add dilute HCl + BaCl₂ → white precipitate of BaSO₄

explanation: Ba²⁺ + SO₄²⁻ → BaSO₄(s) white insoluble sulfate; HCl removes carbonate interference.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Adding silver nitrate (AgNO₃) to chloride solution gives:
explanation: AgCl (white), AgBr (cream), AgI (yellow) - all insoluble silver halides from Ag⁺ + halide.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: How is ammonia gas recognised in a test tube?

options.a: Pungent smell; turns moist red litmus blue
options.b: Colour change of bromothymol blue to yellow

explanation: NH₃ = alkaline gas (pungent smell), turns red litmus blue (NH₃ + H₂O → NH₄⁺ + OH⁻).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: The limewater test for carbon dioxide turns the solution:
explanation: CO₂ + Ca(OH)₂ → CaCO₃↓ (white/milky precipitate).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Why does water rush into a flask in the ammonia fountain experiment?

options.a: NH₃ is highly soluble in water → pressure drop
options.b: Water expands when heated by NH₃

explanation: NH₃ very soluble in water → pressure drops rapidly → water rushes in (fountain).

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
subtopic: Universal indicator full pH range colours
questionText: Universal indicator changes colour across the pH range:

options.a: Red (pH 1) → orange → yellow → green → blue → purple (pH 14)

explanation: Universal indicator covers full pH range with multiple colours 1-14.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Increasing acid concentration in metal-acid reaction generally:
explanation: Higher concentration = more particles per volume = higher collision frequency = faster reaction.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Increasing temperature of a chemical reaction generally:

options.a: Speeds up the reaction (more collisions have energy)

explanation: Higher T = particles have more KE → more collisions have energy ≥ activation → faster.

topic: Chemistry - Acids, Bases and Salts Advanced
questionText: Smaller pieces of solid react faster in a reaction because:

options.a: Larger surface area exposed for collisions per unit mass

explanation: Powder < chips < lumps in surface area exposed → faster reaction (more collision sites).

questionText: What is electrolysis?

options.a: Decomposition of a compound by electricity (molten or aqueous)

explanation: Electrolysis = electrical energy → chemical change (breaks down ionic compound).

questionText: What is an electrolyte?

options.a: Substance that conducts electricity when molten or dissolved (contains mobile ions)

explanation: Electrolyte = substance with free ions that conducts electricity (molten/dissolved ionic compounds).

questionText: At the cathode of an electrolytic cell, what reaction occurs?

options.a: Reduction (gain of electrons, e.g., metal ions + e⁻ → metal)

explanation: Cathode (−) = gain electrons = reduction.

questionText: At the anode of an electrolytic cell during aqueous electrolysis, what is usually produced?

options.a: Oxygen gas (from discharge of OH⁻ or H₂O)

explanation: Anode (+) = loss electrons. With aqueous NaCl/NaOH: OH⁻ discharged → O₂↑ (plus H₂O).

questionText: In electrolysis of molten lead(II) bromide, the products are:

options.a: Pb at cathode (liquid metal), Br₂ at anode (brown vapour)
options.b: Pb at anode, Br₂ at cathode

explanation: Pb²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Pb at cathode. 2Br⁻ → Br₂ + 2e⁻ at anode.

questionText: In the chlor-alkali process (electrolysis of brine NaCl solution), what are the products?

options.a: H₂ at cathode, Cl₂ at anode, NaOH in solution
options.b: Na at cathode, H₂ at anode

explanation: Brine electrolysis: Na⁺ stays; H⁺ + e⁻ → H₂ (cathode); Cl⁻ discharged → Cl₂ (anode); OH⁻ left → NaOH.

questionText: What is the purpose of electroplating?

options.a: To coat a metal with a thin layer of another metal for protection/appearance

explanation: Electroplating = electrolysis where object is cathode → thin metal coat (e.g., Cr on steel).

questionText: To silver-plate a spoon, what should be the electrodes?

options.a: Spoon = cathode (−), silver strip = anode (+), AgNO₃ solution

explanation: Spoon (cathode) to be plated; silver anode dissolves → Ag⁺ → Ag deposits on spoon.

questionText: In electroplating, why is the anode made of the plating metal?

options.a: Anode dissolves providing ions of plating metal to solution

explanation: Active anode (of plating metal) dissolves to replenish ions; cathode gains metal deposit.

questionText: Aluminium is extracted industrially by electrolysis of:

options.a: Molten aluminium oxide (Al₂O₃) dissolved in cryolite

explanation: Al₂O₃ (very high mp ~2050°C) dissolved in cryolite (lowers mp) → electrolysis → Al at cathode.

questionText: What is the overall equation for the electrolysis of molten Al₂O₃?
explanation: Overall: 2Al₂O₃ → 4Al (cathode) + 3O₂ (anode).

questionText: In a Daniell cell (Zn-Cu), zinc is the negative terminal because it:

options.a: Is more reactive, loses electrons more easily than copper
options.c: Does not react with copper ions

explanation: Zn more reactive than Cu → Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻ (anode, − terminal).

questionText: In a simple Zn-Cu electrochemical cell, electrons flow through the external circuit from:
explanation: Electrons flow from anode (Zn, oxidation) → external wire → cathode (Cu, reduction).

questionText: What is the function of a salt bridge (KNO₃) in an electrochemical cell?
explanation: Salt bridge allows ion flow → maintains electrical neutrality → completes circuit.

subtopic: Electrolyte versus non-electrolyte example sodium chloride
questionText: Why is molten sodium chloride a conductor while solid sodium chloride is not?

options.a: Molten NaCl has free mobile ions; solid has ions fixed in lattice
options.b: Solid has no ions at all
options.c: All ionic substances conduct in solid form

explanation: Solid: ions locked in lattice (no conduction). Molten: ions free to move = conduction.

questionText: Which macronutrient provides the most energy per gram?
explanation: Fats = 9 kcal/g; carbs and proteins = 4 kcal/g; vitamins/minerals = 0 kcal/g.

questionText: How many food groups are in Malaysia's balanced diet pyramid (Piramid Makanan)?
explanation: 5 food groups: cereals/tubers; vegetables; fruits; meat/fish/legumes; dairy.

questionText: A student needs 2000 kcal per day. If breakfast provides 25%, breakfast should contain:
explanation: The Basal Metabolic Rate (BMR) is the minimum energy (in kilojoules or kilocalories) the body needs at rest to maintain vital functions (breathing, circulation, body temperature). BMR depends on body mass, age, gender and activity level. For an average adult, BMR is approximately 6,000-7,500 kJ per day.

questionText: Scurvy (bleeding gums, weakness) is caused by deficiency of:
explanation: Vitamin C (ascorbic acid) deficiency = scurvy (was common in sailors).

questionText: Which statement about vitamins is correct?

options.a: Required in small amounts; do not provide energy directly
options.c: Are needed in large gram quantities

explanation: Vitamins = micronutrients, required in small amounts, do NOT provide energy (no calories).

questionText: Rickets (soft weak bones in children) is caused by deficiency of:
explanation: Vitamin D needed for Ca absorption → deficiency = rickets in children (and osteomalacia in adults).

questionText: Which deficiency causes night blindness (poor vision in low light)?
explanation: Vitamin A deficiency = night blindness + xerophthalmia (cornea damage).

questionText: Iron deficiency leads to:
explanation: Iron = essential for haemoglobin → deficiency = anaemia (low Hb, fatigue).

questionText: Iodine deficiency in the diet causes:
explanation: Iodine needed for thyroid hormone (thyroxine) → deficiency = goitre.

subtopic: Calcium deficiency bone and tooth decay
questionText: Which mineral is most associated with healthy bones and teeth?
explanation: Calcium = main mineral in bone (hydroxyapatite) + needed for teeth.

questionText: A child with a swollen belly and muscle wasting, due to severe protein deficiency, may be suffering from:
explanation: Kwashiorkor = severe protein deficiency (oedema/swelling + wasting, common in poor nutrition).

questionText: If daily energy intake equals energy expenditure, body weight will:
explanation: Intake = expenditure → weight stable. Intake > = gain. Intake < = lose.

subtopic: Body mass index BMI calculation category
questionText: Calculate BMI for a person who is 1.6 m tall and weighs 60 kg.
What is the function of dietary fibre (roughage)?
explanation: Fibre (cellulose, indigestible) adds bulk → peristalsis → prevents constipation.

subtopic: Food preservation UHT ultra high temperature technique
questionText: What is UHT (Ultra High Temperature) food treatment?

options.a: Brief heating above 135°C to sterilise food for long storage

explanation: UHT = very brief heating (~135-150°C for 2-5 seconds) sterilises food without major taste change.

questionText: Refrigeration preserves food because:
explanation: Cold temperatures slow metabolism/reproduction of microbes → slows spoilage.

questionText: Salting meat helps preserve it because salt:

options.a: Draws out water (osmotic) creating hostile environment for bacteria

explanation: Salt removes water (high osmotic pressure) → inhibits bacterial growth (water needed for life).

questionText: Which is an example of a food additive used as a preservative?
explanation: Preservatives (e.g., sodium benzoate) extend shelf life by inhibiting microbes.

questionText: Malnutrition in young children most commonly affects:
explanation: Malnutrition → stunted growth, weak immunity, higher mortality in children.

questionText: Severe dehydration in a child may cause:
explanation: Severe dehydration = lethargy, sunken fontanelle/eyes, dry mucous membranes.

questionText: A balanced diet helps prevent:
explanation: Balanced diet + exercise = prevention of obesity, type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular diseases.

subtopic: Cholesterol dietary source animal versus plant
questionText: Which food is highest in saturated fats and cholesterol?
explanation: Animal products (butter, eggs, fatty meats) = saturated fats + dietary cholesterol.

questionText: Which type of dietary fat is most healthy for the heart?
explanation: Unsaturated fats (mono + poly) lower LDL → better for cardiovascular health.

subtopic: Glycemic index type 1 versus type 2 diabetes
questionText: Foods with high glycemic index cause:
explanation: High GI foods = quickly digested → rapid blood glucose spike.

subtopic: BMR body energy requirement at rest explained
questionText: What does BMR (basal metabolic rate) actually measure in the body?

options.a: Energy needed at rest to maintain vital functions
options.c: Total daily calories from food only

explanation: BMR = energy needed at complete rest (basic life functions, breathing, circulation).

subtopic: BMI formula weight height calculation example
questionText: If someone weighs 70 kg and is 1.75 m tall, what is their BMI (use kg/m²)?
One Calorie (food) equals how many kilojoules?
explanation: 1 kcal ≈ 4.184 kJ (≈ 4.2 kJ). Food labels in Malaysia show both kcal and kJ.

questionText: Which form of carbohydrate gives the quickest release of energy to the body?
explanation: Simple sugars (glucose) require no digestion → absorbed fastest into bloodstream for energy.

questionText: A BMI of 32 indicates:
explanation: BMI ≥30 = obesity → increased risk of type 2 diabetes, hypertension, CVD.

questionText: WHO recommends at least how many servings of fruits and vegetables daily?
explanation: WHO: minimum 5 portions of fruits/vegetables daily (≈400g) for healthy diet.

questionText: How many millimetres are in 3.5 cm?
When reading a measuring cylinder, how should the reading be recorded?

options.a: To one figure beyond the smallest scale division (estimated digit)

explanation: Record to 1/10 of smallest division (best estimate + precise digits). E.g., 25.0 mL if smallest division is 1 mL.

questionText: Which of these is a vector quantity?
explanation: Vector = magnitude + direction. Velocity is vector. Speed is scalar.

questionText: How is measurement uncertainty (random error) reduced?
explanation: Repeating and averaging reduces random errors (precision improves).

questionText: A zero error in a measuring instrument is an example of:
explanation: Systematic error = consistent error (e.g., zero not set correctly). Same direction each time.

subtopic: Acceleration unit m per s squared
questionText: The SI unit of acceleration is:
explanation: Acceleration = velocity change / time → m/s / s = m/s².

questionText: One newton is the force that gives a mass of 1 kg an acceleration of:
explanation: By Newton's 2nd law: 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m/s².

questionText: The mass of an electron is about 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg. What is this in regular notation?
explanation: 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ = 0.0000...911 (31 zeros after decimal).

questionText: To avoid parallax error when reading a measuring cylinder, the eye should be:

options.a: Level with the bottom of the meniscus

explanation: Parallax error = reading from above/below → read eye-level with liquid meniscus.

questionText: Measurements are precise but not accurate. This means:

options.a: Measurements cluster together but are far from true value

explanation: Precision = how close measurements are to each other. Accuracy = closeness to true value.

questionText: A car accelerates from rest at 2 m/s² for 5 seconds. Final velocity = ?
On a distance-time graph, a horizontal straight line indicates:
explanation: Horizontal line = no change in distance over time = stationary.

subtopic: Velocity time graph area under curve distance
questionText: What does the area under a velocity-time graph represent?
explanation: Area under v-t graph = displacement/distance travelled (integration).

subtopic: Newton second law F equals ma calculation
questionText: A 1500 kg car accelerates at 3 m/s². Net force = ?
All objects in free fall near Earth's surface accelerate at approximately:
explanation: g ≈ 9.8 m/s² (≈10 m/s²) for all objects in vacuum (air resistance ignored).

questionText: In projectile motion (ignoring air resistance), horizontal velocity:
explanation: Horizontally: no acceleration (no horizontal force). Vertical: g downward.

questionText: An object is dropped from rest. How long does it take to fall 20 m? (g = 10 m/s²)
A 2 kg ball moving at 3 m/s has momentum:
explanation: Momentum (p) is the product of mass and velocity: p = m x v (kg*m/s). Impulse is the change in momentum: J = F x t = Δp. The impulse-momentum theorem states that a force applied over a time interval changes an object's momentum by an amount equal to the impulse.

questionText: What is the relationship between impulse and momentum?

options.a: Impulse = change in momentum (F × t = Δp)

explanation: Impulse = F × Δt = Δp (change in momentum).

questionText: Conservation of momentum applies when:

options.a: Net external force on system is zero

explanation: Conservation of momentum = no external force on isolated system.

questionText: In an elastic collision:

options.a: Both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved

explanation: Elastic = kinetic energy + momentum conserved (e.g., ideal gas molecules).

questionText: When two objects collide and stick together, this is:
explanation: Perfectly inelastic = objects combine (stick); max KE lost, momentum still conserved.

subtopic: Newton third law action reaction pair
questionText: A person weighing 60 kg stands on floor. The force exerted by the floor on the person is:
explanation: Normal force = W = mg = 60 × 9.8 = 588 N upward (Newton's 3rd law: floor pushes up).

questionText: Work done by a force = :
explanation: Work = Force × displacement × cos(angle between F and s).

questionText: A motor does 1000 J of work in 5 s. Its power is:
explanation: Power P = W/t (work done per unit time). For W = 1000 J and t = 5 s: P = 1000/5 = 200 W. SI unit of power is the watt (W), where 1 W = 1 J/s. Electrical power: P = VI = I^2 R = V^2/R.

subtopic: Kinetic energy formula 1/2 m v squared
questionText: A 1000 kg car moves at 20 m/s. Its kinetic energy is:
A 5 kg object is lifted 3 m. GPE gained = (g = 10 m/s²)

subtopic: Work energy theorem W = Δ KE
questionText: When net work is done on an object, it equals:
explanation: Work-energy theorem: W = ΔKE (net work = change in kinetic energy).

questionText: A single fixed pulley is used to lift a load. What is its mechanical advantage (MA)?
explanation: Fixed pulley = MA = 1 (changes direction of force but no force multiplication).

questionText: Pressure is defined as:
